ov: Cartilaginous fish with five to seven gill slits on each side and rows of replaceable teeth. More than 470 species range from the 17 cm dwarf lanternshark to the whale shark, the largest fish in the world.

why.dg: Only four of more than 470 species, the great white, oceanic whitetip, tiger and bull sharks, are behind a significant number of fatal, unprovoked attacks.
why.et: Sharks are caught for their meat and their fins.

len: 17 cm (dwarf lanternshark) to over 12 m (whale shark)
rg: All seas, commonly down to 2,000 m. A few, such as the bull shark and the river sharks, can also live in fresh water.
df: Most hunt fish and other sea animals, but the biggest species, the whale and basking sharks, filter plankton from the water.
fx: Most sharks give birth to live young: the eggs hatch inside the mother before the pups are born.
